$comment: Curated cross-engine rule equivalences. Two issues on the same path and start line from different engines are duplicates when their rules share a CWE or are listed here. Keep this small and reviewed: every entry states why it is safe. The eslint:sonarjs/<name> pairs at the end are generated by tools/analyzers/sonarjs/own-pairs.mjs --write (one per eslint-plugin-sonarjs 2.0.4 rule) and replaced wholesale when it runs.

gitleaks.reason: Every Gitleaks rule detects a hard-coded credential (CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials), but Gitleaks SARIF carries no CWE, so without this a Gitleaks finding could never share a CWE with the Semgrep secret rules that report the same line.

pairs.reason: Both flag a direct eval() call; ESLint's rule metadata carries no CWE. PENDING VERIFICATION: a person must confirm the Semgrep rule id against the Semgrep registry before this entry is relied on.

Both report an array access outside its bounds.
Both report if/else branches with identical code.
Both report the same expression on both sides of an operator.
Both report a variable used after it was moved from.
